subject: Follow-up: SLO scoping, streaming requirements & reproducibility sprint
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jmiller@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: SLO scoping, streaming requirements & reproducibility sprint

Hi Jordan / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get BrightCart qualified on performance SLOs: 

Summary of asks from your side
- Latency targets: p95 <= 120 ms for short single-turn responses (<= 256 tokens), p99 <= 300 ms for longer generations up to 1k tokens.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state 150 QPS with spikes to 400 QPS for seasonal peaks.
- Concurrency: expected 250 concurrent active connections for shopping assistant flows.
- Streaming: token-level streaming for conversation transcripts; you noted clients expect token-chunk latency <= 50 ms for perceived real-time.

What we propose
1) Measurement definitions: we will measure p50/p95/p99 generation latency (client send -> final token), and token-chunk latency for streaming (first token latency + inter-token gaps).
2) Repro sprint: 3 days of runs on a dedicated benchmark pool mirroring your target concurrency and QPS. We will provide the harness and a reproducibility playbook.
3) Prompt/eval artifacts: please share the representative prompt-set and sample traffic (anonymized). We can also accept replay traces (timestampped requests) or synthetic load based on your distributions.
4) Acceptance criteria: we’ll draft an SLO acceptance doc for you to sign off.

Attachments: I’ve attached the prompt set you dropped on the call (BrightCart_demo_prompt_set_v1.json) and a quick checklist.

Next steps / asks
- Jordan / Priya: confirm the prompt-set above is final or tell us the Drive link for updated examples.
- Confirm if you can provide a replay trace or if we should synthesize traffic from the prompts.
- Ben / Marcus: can you scope the repro sprint and propose 2 dates next week?

Thanks — I’ll assemble the mutual action plan once we have answers to the three bullets above.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sofia — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Streaming behavior: our client expects incremental transcript chunks every ~150ms; our frontend will buffer for 2 chunks before rendering. For your measurement, token-chunk latency <= 75ms between emitted chunks would be acceptable given network variance.

2) Workload: we can share a 48-hour replay trace (anonymized) that contains peaks of ~420 QPS. We can also provide a shorter representative traffic sample (10k requests) for quick repro runs. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2BcDemoPrompts

3) Test accounts: we can stand up a test api-key scoped to non-prod and allow IP allowlist for the Redwood bench pool.

I’m attaching the representative prompt file and a short README. We’d prefer Redwood run the initial repro using our replay trace so we can validate the end-to-end path.

Jordan

Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO scoping, streaming requirements & reproducibility sprint

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Jordan. A few notes on how we’ll operationalize measurement so the results are reproducible and comparable to your production metrics: 

Measurement definitions (proposal)
- Generation latency (closed-form): measured at the bench client as time delta from request POST to receipt of final token byte. This will be reported as p50/p95/p99 across runs and broken down by token-length buckets (<=256, 257-1024, >1024).
- Streaming latency: two signals — first-token latency (time to first token) and inter-token gap (median/99th of chunk-to-chunk intervals). We will emit time-series at 10ms resolution.
- Throughput stability: measure sustained QPS over sliding 60s windows; we will compute variance and tail spikes.

Repro strategy
- Use your 48h replay trace for a full run (we’ll replay at original timing once on a dedicated pool).
- Synthetic stress runs: scale the replay to 150% to validate headroom and collect degradation curves.
- Environment capture: bench will snapshot model variant, quantization flags, GPU type, kernel-selection logs, and runtime config; we will store artifacts in the run bundle for later replay.

Action items
- Ben: scope the bench environment and provide target dates (2 options).
- Jordan: share the test api-key or a temporary allowlist IP range by EOD Friday so we can stage the pool.
- Sofia: I’ll draft the measurement-spec.csv and repro-playbook-v1.md and circulate for review.

Karthik
Director, Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Priya — thanks for the replay trace link. Proposed repro sprint plan and checklist below (high level):

Day 0 (prep)
- Confirm test api-key / IP allowlist.
- Stage bench pool (N=6 GPUs, A100 equivalent) and pin model:v2-q4f16.
- Validate that replay trace plays back and map endpoints to Redwood routes.

Day 1 (baseline)
- Run replay at original timing, collect p50/p95/p99, first-token and inter-token gaps.
- Run small synthetic run at 150 QPS to validate harness.

Day 2 (stress and scaling)
- Scale to 150% then 250% of observed peaks (up to 420 QPS) to build degradation curves.
- Capture runtime artifacts and kernel-selection logs.

Deliverables
- repro-playbook-v1.md (run checklist and steps)
- measurement-spec.csv (columns: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, token_count, first_token_ms, inter_token_gap_ms)
- run-bundles (artifact tarballs) for each run

Dates: we can run the prep + baseline + stress on Tue/Wed/Thu next week (Dec 15-17) or Mon/Tue/Wed (Dec 14-16). Which do you prefer?

Ben Carter
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: repro-playbook-v1.md (text/markdown)
Attachment: measurement-spec.csv (text/csv)

P.S. Marcus — I’ll need help with kernel-selection logs collection and packaging. Can you confirm availability?
